01 / 08
Curatorial Thesis · Mineral Memory

Industrial runoff and optical fiber conduits form a single stratigraphic layer. The biennale interrogates how matter registers loss, transformation, and planetary memory.

Subterranean Archives

Solid matter, core extraction samples, and radioactive ceramic residues detailing extractive history.

Hydrological Signals

Tidal sedimentation, toxic runoff flows, and multi-channel acoustic drift across estuarine zones.

Post-Carbon Poetics

Mycorrhizal bioreactors and computational ecologies proposing regenerative architectural futures.

LUMEN & SILT · Curatorial Brief · October 2026
02 / 08
Spatial Choreography · 4 Pavilions
Rooms
Four distinct atmospheric thresholds designed to separate acoustic frequencies, manage light decay, and control narrative pacing across 75 minutes.
Pavilion · Environment · Experience
01

Room I: Suspension (Atrium)

Natural raw daylight, low-lux acoustic dampening, monumental suspended copper slag and saline textiles.

02

Room II: The Core Sample (North Gallery)

Geological core specimen vitrines, subterranean drilling archives, low directional tungsten lighting.

03

Room III: Hydrological Drift (South Hall)

Dual-channel water-table projections, floor-mounted acoustic transducers, damp acoustic resonance.

04

Room IV: Terminal Bloom (Vaults)

Zero daylight immersion, living bioluminescent algae bioreactors, synthetic fungal network soundscapes.

Trevor Paglen & Forensic Architecture

Hito Steyerl

Dual-channel simulated liquidation of speculative rare-earth and semiconductor minerals.
